clue.text: Concerned with teeth …

parts.note: a plain description of an adjective relating to the teeth, opening a chain of clues joined by ellipses about toothless animals

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is a dental term built on the Greek root for tooth, meaning relating to teeth.

clue.text: Cheat, full of holes with change of ends

indicators.note: the end letters of the word for full of holes swap places, the first going last and the last first

parts.note: something full of holes is riddled, as with bullets

explanation.surface: A swindler is exposed, his story full of holes, as he keeps switching his tale from one end to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with change of ends' swaps the first and last letters, so the R at the front and the D at the back trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: A diddler is an informal British word for a swindler, someone who cheats people out of money.

clue.text: Chapel rather than church for the time being?

parts.note: chapel-goers in Britain were Nonconformists, defined by being non-Church of England, so this phrase gives the prefix meaning not
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone attends chapel instead of church, but only temporarily.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'chapel' traditionally meant the Nonconformist (Protestant, non-Anglican) churches, as opposed to the Church of England, CE. The phrase 'for the nonce' means for the time being.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonce is an old noun for the present occasion, used in the idiom for the nonce, meaning for now.

clue.text: Citizen is artist and priest

parts.note: taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
Eli is the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A list of someone's roles: a citizen who is both a painter and a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: RA (Royal Academician) and ELI (the biblical priest) are both crossword stand-bys.
explanation.definitionFit: A national of the state of Israel is a citizen of that country.

clue.text: … one dentally challenged (when it follows, appeal to refrain from the intolerable), formerly classed in …

annotationWithheld.why: '… one dentally challenged (when it follows, appeal to refrain from the intolerable), formerly classed in …': 'one dentally challenged' defines ANTBEAR, but the parenthetical aside (ANT BEAR + IT as a plea about the intolerable) gives no wordplay the grammar can express, and 'formerly classed in' belongs to the 10/27 chain
annotationWithheld.clue: … one dentally challenged (when it follows, appeal to refrain from the intolerable), formerly classed in …

clue.text: Adverse decision of video referee without a lawyer

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the ruling wraps round the a

parts.note: in rugby the video referee may rule no try, disallowing a score

explanation.surface: A rugby video referee rules against a score without consulting a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: NO TRY goes round A. The video referee (television match official) in rugby union decides whether a try was scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary is a legal official who certifies documents, a kind of lawyer.

clue.text: Take my tip: small ball's against the other side

parts.note: a bead is a small ball, as on a necklace
v, short for versus, means against

indicators.note: an other version of the word side is a rearrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports tip: a little ball is in play against the opposing team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' turns SIDE into ISED; the 's is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: Be advised is a phrase of warning or counsel, offering advice like saying listen to me.

clue.text: Worm with most of a sidecar inside

indicators.note: the car part of sidecar is moved to sit inside what remains of a side
most of a side is the phrase with its final letter dropped, leaving the rest

parts.note: taken as written: read as side plus car

explanation.surface: A worm is found inside a motorcycle sidecar.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'a sidecar' as A SIDE + CAR: 'most of' cuts A SIDE to ASID, and 'inside' puts CAR within it, AS(CAR)ID.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascarid is a parasitic roundworm, such as the large intestinal worm of humans and pigs.

clue.text: Star of the bench takes part of course: the whole may ruin reform

parts.note: a leg is one stage of a course or journey
the whole is all of it

indicators.note: to reform is to shape anew, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: A sporting judge takes part in a course, but fears the whole thing may wreck a reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges MAY RUIN into UMINARY; 'takes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal luminary is an eminent judge or lawyer, a shining figure of the bench.

clue.text: … Paradise Lost

annotationWithheld.why: '… Paradise Lost (8)' with 27: EDEN (Paradise) + TATA (Lost, as a goodbye) gives EDENTATA, but the clue has no definition of its own; it comes from 5-across's 'formerly classed in', and 'Lost' as TATA cannot be honestly glossed

clue.text: Coming back, but never coming back to unconsciousness

indicators.note: the second coming back says the word for never is read from right to left

parts.note: ne'er is a poetic contraction of never
a trance is a state of semi-consciousness or unconsciousness

explanation.surface: Someone returning, though never expected to come back to consciousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' (the second time) turns NEER into REEN; 'to' only joins it to TRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A re-entrance is the act of entering again, a return.

clue.text: Record protection maybe for heart

definitions.meaning: the paper or card cover that protects a vinyl record
the place for the heart in wearing one's heart on one's ...

explanation.surface: Cover for a record, and the place a romantic displays his heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeve is both a record's cover and, in an idiom, where emotions are worn openly.

clue.text: One of 10 27 gives a US university, topped and turned, £1000

indicators.note: turned means the remaining letters are churned round into a new order
topped means having the head cut off, so the first letter of the university goes

parts.note: Harvard is a famous US university
K, for kilo, means a thousand, a grand

explanation.surface: One of a group of animals somehow yields an American university, upside down, and a grand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' removes H from HARVARD, and 'turned' rearranges ARVARD into ARDVAR. 10 27 is EDENTATA, a former order of toothless mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: The aardvark, the African ant-eating burrower, was formerly classified among the edentates.

clue.text: One of 10 27, one right out of mind and sick with love

parts.note: a means one
out of one's mind means mad
ill means sick
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An animal is out of its mind and lovesick.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo, a South American armoured mammal, was traditionally grouped with the edentates.

clue.text: A tough problem assuming responsibility for signature

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the shuffled word takes the responsibility inside it
a problem with the word tough leaves its letters messed up and reordered

parts.note: taken as written as fodder
the rap is the blame or responsibility, as in take the rap

explanation.surface: A hard task: taking on responsibility for a signature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' looks like part of the definition phrase but is the anagram signal, and 'assuming' (taking on) is the container signal; 'take the rap' means accept the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: An autograph is a person's own handwritten signature.

clue.text: Wrong ideas concealed from rest of cast?

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of the next word are set out in an incorrect order

explanation.surface: Mistaken notions are kept from the other actors.
explanation.definitionFit: On stage, a remark spoken to the audience that the other characters supposedly cannot hear.

clue.text: One of 10 27 is a sin

definitions.meaning: one of the edentates, a slow tree-hanging South American mammal
one of the seven deadly sins, laziness

explanation.surface: One animal is itself a deadly sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth names both the slow-moving tree mammal and the deadly sin of idleness.

clue.text: One making some money should have a plate put up

definitions.text: One making some money should have a plate put up

parts.note: an L-plate, the red L on white that British ... drivers must display
an earner makes money

explanation.surface: A newcomer earning a little money should mount a nameplate.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain learner drivers must display L-plates, so the L goes on top of EARNER and the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner driver is the one who must show an L-plate on the car.

clue.text: One politician, sound in record, falling suddenly towards the centre

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
MP is Member of Parliament

indicators.note: in places the noise inside the record

parts.note: a log is a record, as a ship's log
din is a loud sound

explanation.surface: A politician making noise on the record suddenly falls in on himself.
explanation.definitionFit: To implode is to collapse violently inwards, the opposite of exploding.

clue.text: Speaker embracing nude characters one after another

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the lip wraps round the other letters

parts.note: the lip, part of the mouth, is an organ of speech

indicators.note: characters here means the letters of the word nude taken loose and set in a new order

explanation.surface: A speaker is embracing naked characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' suggests the Commons Speaker, but here it is a part of the mouth; 'characters' asks for the letters of the next word rearranged, and 'embracing' wraps them.
explanation.definitionFit: Things lined up stand in a row, arranged in sequence one after another.

clue.text: Ribbon development on isthmus needs link

parts.note: a neck of land is an isthmus
a tie is a link or bond

explanation.surface: Building strung along a narrow strip of land needs a connection.
explanation.walkthrough: Ribbon development is British for houses built in a line along a road; here it is read as a ribbon developed into neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is a strip of fabric worn round the neck, a ribbon grown into clothing.

clue.text: Continue to lose energy and bottle

parts.note: to flag is to tire or lose energy
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: Going on until you tire and reach for the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large bottle or jug for wine or ale.

clue.text: One of 10 27 from African country not complete in number

indicators.note: in puts the shortened country inside the number

parts.note: a PIN is a personal identification number

indicators.note: not complete means the last letter of the country is dropped

parts.note: Angola is a country in south-west Africa

explanation.surface: One animal comes from an African country, numbers incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: The pangolin, or scaly anteater, was formerly grouped with the edentates.

clue.text: Subtle point for actor Tom to abandon extension

indicators.note: to abandon means the actor's name leaves the longer word

parts.note: a continuance is an extension in time
Tom Conti is a Scottish stage and screen actor

explanation.surface: A fine distinction lets an actor walk away from a contract extension.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Conti is a Scottish actor known for Shirley Valentine.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle shade of meaning or difference.

clue.text: Old American sleuth pursuing extremes

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the detective comes after

parts.note: A to Z are the extremes of the alphabet
tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: An old American detective chases after outer limits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs were a native people of ancient Mexico, an old American civilisation.

clue.text: The last sin, journalists without money: we must try and save them

definitions.text: we must try and save them

parts.note: the end is the last part
anger, or wrath, is one of the deadly sins

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the journalists go round the money

parts.note: eds are editors, journalists
specie is money in coin

explanation.surface: The last sin of broke journalists: something we must try to rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, the container signal; 'specie' is coin money, and 'try and save them' describes conservationists' aim.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservation efforts aim to save animals and plants at risk of extinction.

clue.text: See 10
Deprived people in favour of backing German

indicators.note: backing means the word is read backwards

parts.note: pro means in favour of
Hans is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: Backing a German in favour of the deprived.
explanation.definitionFit: Orphans are deprived of their parents.
